title: Building Block Three: The Job No Leader Should Delegate
coreMove: Face role fit directly enough to move the right person into the work the strategy actually needs.
sourcePressure: Third building block: getting the right people in the right jobs is non-delegable because comfort, weak knowledge, and lack of courage keep mismatches alive. No chapter-specific employee case is frozen.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turn people decisions into generic hiring tips or harsh performance-management talk.

hook: the building block three: the job no leader should delegate that nobody sees until it is too late
a meeting room where every plan sounds good
a generic promise colliding with reality
counterintuition: Most leaders think X, but the opposite is true
The problem is not effort, it is discipline
Execution is not about working harder
tryThisNow: set a timer and write three priorities
audit one goal in your notebook
ask yourself what matters most today
examples: generic project kickoff with vague owners
student team with a deadline and no specificity
family calendar scene used as a management analogy

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional pharmacy chain deciding whether a beloved store manager can handle controlled-substance compliance
exampleSpecs.stakes: loyalty to a warm manager can expose patients and licenses to risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire separates affection from role fit by putting audit failures beside the compliance demands of the job
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The controlled-substance cabinet clicks shut while Claire reads the third missed reconciliation note.

exampleSpecs.domain: a film festival assigning a volunteer director for sponsor logistics
exampleSpecs.stakes: a crowd favorite can lose sponsor commitments if he cannot follow through through others
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Jack asks for evidence that the candidate gets work done through others before letting popularity decide the assignment
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Who has he actually moved besides himself?" Jack asks while the sponsor map lies between them.

exampleSpecs.domain: a dental practice deciding whether a technically strong hygienist should lead the new-patient flow
exampleSpecs.stakes: a clinical star may not energize assistants or solve tough handoffs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Manon replaces vague admiration with four role-fit criteria: energizes people, decides tough issues, works through others, follows through
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Manon two missed new-patient handoffs to stop calling technical skill the whole job.

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional construction firm choosing a superintendent for a hospital wing
exampleSpecs.audience: an owner who dislikes hard placement conversations
exampleSpecs.stakes: the wrong superintendent can make subcontractor coordination fail under inspection pressure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mathieu names the psychological comfort factor when he realizes he is keeping an easy relationship in a hard job
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The hospital-wing punch list runs three pages, and Mathieu keeps looking at the name he wants to protect.

exampleSpecs.domain: a university language department moving an admired lecturer into program administration
exampleSpecs.stakes: students can lose course continuity if warmth substitutes for decisive administration
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marta predicts which unresolved decision will expose the mismatch, then asks for unvarnished truth before assigning the role
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which matters more for the program next semester: beloved lectures or the courage to cut a course?

exampleSpecs.domain: a Toronto logistics startup deciding whether the founder should keep a friend as head of carrier relations
exampleSpecs.stakes: personal comfort can block the carrier network the strategy needs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lin writes down what she knows, what she is avoiding, and what role the business actually needs before making the people decision herself
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You have the carrier complaints in one tab and Lin has the old friendship thread in another.

skillTargets: diagnose lack of knowledge, courage, comfort, and personal commitment in people decisions
choose evidence of role fit over affection or popularity
separate execution qualities from vague talent admiration
evaluate when unvarnished truth is needed

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one role you influence and write the job demands first, then the person you feel most comfortable naming for it.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
